Evidence

MOSSLINK / A FICTIONAL PORTFOLIO STUDY

01 / THE QUESTION

Between code
and the bench.

How do you connect a firmware decision to something you can actually observe?

I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture for Mosslink, an environmental sensor.

Firmware is code that controls a physical device.
↓
Follow the work

02 / THE SCHEDULE

Low power is
a schedule.

I scheduled the firmware's power states. This teaching loop separates a device's work into three states.

01
Sleep
Wait between work.
02
Measure
Take a reading.
03
Transmit
Send a report.

↶ Then back to Sleep.

Explanatory teaching loop, not Mosslink's actual firmware. No timings or current values are shown.

My working documents include state tables, timing diagrams and bench checklists: ways to describe the work to check.

03 / THE BENCH

From a command
to a check.

Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation. My fixture makes its response available to bench instruments.

01
Command
02
Board
03
Fixture
04
Observe

Ada wrote the firmware and scheduled its power states. State tables and timing diagrams are part of her working documents; this is not a reproduction of that firmware.

I wrote the firmware and built the fixture. A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end.

Command → board → fixture → observation.
An explanatory relationship, not electrical wiring.

04 / THE EVIDENCE

Two numbers.
Different evidence.
INPUTS TO AN ESTIMATE

MEASURED
Sleep and transmit current on the bench.

+

ASSUMED
The reporting interval.

→
2 years
Projected battery life

A SEPARATE OBSERVATION

A continuous run on the bench.

→
72 hours
The longest observed run

Authored explanation of the supplied fictional notes, not the original spreadsheet or a measured trace. The run does not establish two years of operation.

An estimate is not two years of observed operation.

05 / THE SCOPE

A connection.
Not a leap.

I connect firmware decisions to bench observations through power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture, while keeping the evidence limits visible.

Engineering samples assembled
40
Tested on the bench
6
Sent to customers
0
Six highlighted cells mark the bench-tested subset of forty. This illustrative count is not a pass/fail chart.

One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.

Read the source and limits
↘

FROM THE SUPPLIED NOTES

The source behind
the story.
“Battery spreadsheet uses measured sleep and transmit current with an assumed reporting interval.”

From the fictional Mosslink lab notes. The spreadsheet, current values and reporting interval are not supplied.

Back to the question ↑

The longest run was 72 hours. Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle.

Forty engineering samples were assembled. Six were tested on the bench. None went to customers.

One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.

Ada wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture. A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end.

Ada and Mosslink are fictional. Illustrative bench model: shapes and connections are explanatory, not a photograph, circuit diagram, wiring plan or measured signal.
